hotspots.label: Protein coat
hotspots.description: The outer protein shell of the virus that holds and protects the genetic material.
hotspots.positionHint: The outer capsule layer of the viral particle.
hotspots.function: Protects and carries the genes inside.

hotspots.label: Genetic material
hotspots.description: The DNA or RNA inside the virus that carries its genes - the blueprint for making more viruses.
hotspots.positionHint: The coiled strand inside the coat.

hotspots.label: Attachment spikes
hotspots.description: Protein spikes on the outside that help the virus attach to a specific host cell.
hotspots.positionHint: Short projections poking from the coat surface.
hotspots.function: Stick the virus to its target cell.

hotspots.label: Host cell
hotspots.description: A living cell the virus invades, using the cell's machinery to build more viruses.
hotspots.positionHint: The larger adjacent cell the viral particles are moving toward.
hotspots.function: Provides machinery for the virus to copy itself.

visualStyleNotes: Anatomy Atelier best: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A calm, clean stylized diorama. Muted, not gamey; glowing color used sparingly - the protein coat a refined neutral with restrained contrast, nothing luminous. Strong saturated color only on the small flat hotspot dots.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0, matte roughness ~0.55-0.65. The coat is a clean surface, no emissive.
assetBrief: SUBJECT: a single icosahedral (capsule-ball) virus centrally placed, with a clean protein outer coat, visible internal genetic strand, and a few surface attachment spikes. A second larger host cell sits to one side, and a reproduction layer animates new small viruses emerging. Muted palette on warm cream. Named nodes: VirusCoat, GeneticStrand, Spikes, HostCell, NewVirusDots. Budget 12-16k.
